others.route: Work permit (Jersey Customs and Immigration Service) and visa

note: Jersey: everyone who isn't British or Irish needs immigration permission to visit, work, study or settle, and an employer must apply for a work permit, under the Immigration (Work Permits) (Jersey) Rules 1995, for anyone who needs that permission to come or stay for work; British and Irish citizens need no permit (Government of Jersey, Work Permit Policy, updated January 2026). Entertainers holding a UK Tier 5 temporary worker visa may perform in Jersey for up to a month without a work permit, and those staying longer or coming straight from overseas may need a work permit and a visa: the form can't hold a rule that turns on another country's visa, so no days are modelled. Those with EU settled or pre-settled status and the policy's other exempt classes aren't modelled apart. Read in archive.org's snapshot of 19 May 2026, since gov.je's firewall blocks this client.

sources.title: Government of Jersey, Work Permit Policy (updated January 2026; archive.org snapshot of 19 May 2026)
sources.said: All persons who are not British or Irish require immigration permission to visit, work, study or settle in Jersey. ... Work permits are a requirement under the Immigration (Work Permits) (Jersey) Rules 1995 and as such employers are required to apply for a work permit for those individuals who require immigration permission to enter or remain in Jersey for work. ... Employees do not require a permit to work in Jersey if they are: a British or Irish citizen ... Entertainers in possession of a UK Tier 5 Temporary Worker visa can work in Jersey as a performer for up to 1 month without the need for a work permit.
